source.publication: Tax Treatment of Government Pensions (Massachusetts DOR web page, updated April 3, 2026)
source.section: 'Tier I and II railroad retirement pension': 'Tier I or Tier II railroad retirement benefits are exempt from Massachusetts taxation.' Form 1 lines 2a, 2c, 4, 10-22 (2025 Form 1 Instructions PDF p10, p12)

worked: Federal AGI = Tier II railroad retirement annuity (federally taxable part, Form RRB-1099-R) 24,000.00 (person 0) + private pension 36,000.00 (person 0) = 60,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - 17,750.00 standard deduction (15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 or older) = 42,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 0.00 for the 24,000.00 Tier II railroad retirement annuity (federally taxable part, Form RRB-1099-R) (exempt: 'Tier I or Tier II railroad retirement benefits are exempt from Massachusetts taxation', Tax Treatment of Government Pensions) + 36,000.00 private pension (taxed: most private pensions are taxable, PDF p10) = 36,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 36,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 36,000.00 - 0.00 = 36,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (single) = 4,400.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 1 x 700.00 = 700.00; line 2g = line 18 = 5,100.00. Line 19 = 36,000.00 - 5,100.00 = 30,900.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 30,900.00. Line 22 = 30,900.00 x 0.05 = 1,545.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 1,545.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 36,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 1,545.00.
